Keith knows that Elizabeth has been curt, but after Scenario 1 he learns it is due to personal stress rather than anger at him. In Scenario 2, she accepts his support and coffee break. By Scenario 3, Elizabeth shares more about her stress, and Keith knows it seems severe enough that professional help might benefit her. He also knows she is hesitant about seeking help from her response.

Keith does **not** know the full details of her personal stress beyond what she shares, nor does he yet know whether his suggestion will feel offensive or embarrassing to her. That concern is only his worry, not a known fact, until Scenario 4 when he notices her withdrawal.

In Scenario 3, Keith’s actual action is raising the topic of professional help carefully through his dialogue: “Have you considered talking to a professional?” This best matches “Carefully broaches the subject of seeking professional advice.”
